Second, the definition of "passenger automobile", unlike the definition of "automobile" is not identical to existing definitions in other statutes with established interpretations. Third, since all automobiles carry at least one passenger, interpreting primarily to mean "substantial" would result in no automobile being classified as a nonpassenger automobile. Since Congress clearly intended that nonpassenger automobiles be considered apart from passenger automobiles, such an interpretation would defeat a clear Congressional intent.

Captive Imports. In the NPRM, the NHTSA indicated its tentative intent to calculate a single average fuel economy figure for domestic manufacturers which have captive imports by combining the captive imports with the domestically produced vehicles of those manufacturers. Captive imports are vehicles, such as the Chevrolet LUV and the Ford Courier pickup trucks, which are marketed by a domestic manufacturer but fabricated by a foreign manufacturer. It is anticipated that approximately 50,000 1979 LUV's and 50,000 1979 Couriers will be imported into this country.
